'''''War''''' (stylised in [[all caps]]) is a [[legal drama]] [[Anthology series|anthology]] television series created by [[George Kay (writer)|George Kay]]. The show premiered on 1 October 2026, on [[HBO]] in the United States and on the following night on [[Sky Atlantic]] in the United Kingdom.

==Premise==
The first season is about two prestigious law firms in London, "Cathcarts" and "Taylor & Byrne," as they face off in a scandalous divorce case between a tech entrepreneur and his film star wife.<ref>{{cite web|website=Variety|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/global/dominic-west-sienna-miller-war-series-hbo-sky-1236493739/|title=Dominic West and Sienna Miller to Star in Legal Thriller Series ''War'' at HBO and Sky, Season 2 Already Greenlit|date=Aug 20, 2025|accessdate=Aug 20, 2025|first=Ellise|last=Shafer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250820150309/https://variety.com/2025/tv/global/dominic-west-sienna-miller-war-series-hbo-sky-1236493739|archive-date=20 August 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

The second season follows the two rival law firms as they take on an explosive [[defamation]] case.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|website=The Hollywood Reporter|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/marisa-tomei-kelly-macdonald-david-harewood-war-season-2-1236589097/|title=Marisa Tomei, Kelly Macdonald, David Harewood Board Season 2 of Sky and HBO Legal Drama ‘War’|date=7 May 2026|accessdate=8 May 2026|first=Lily|last=Ford|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508020438/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/marisa-tomei-kelly-macdonald-david-harewood-war-season-2-1236589097/|archive-date=8 May 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

 |Title           = It's Done
 |DirectedBy      = Ben Taylor
 |WrittenBy       = [[George Kay (writer)|George Kay]]

 |ShortSummary    = Morgan Henderson, the [[London]]-based CEO of social media site Zephyr, sleeps with a young woman named Flora he meets after an award show. Unbeknownst to him, Flora is a friend of his estranged wife and film star Carla Duval, who set up the encounter as a [[Honey trapping|honey trap]] to use against her divorce case. In [[Paris]] for the premiere of her newest film ''The Milliner'', Carla meets with her lawyers Nicholas Taylor and Serena Byrne to discuss her plans to divorce Morgan. Nicholas and Serena are the married partners of law firm Taylor & Byrne, whose sworn rival is nearby law firm Cathcarts, of which Morgan keeps on retainer and Serena used to work for. After seeing pictures of Carla's meeting in a [[Tabloid journalism|tabloid]] rag, Morgan contacts Cathcarts partner St. John Smallwood; he is unworried due to the air-tight [[prenuptial agreement]] they signed before marrying, but still decides to mount his own divorce case against Carla. Johnny Warren, a working-class young man from a [[Public housing in the United Kingdom|council estate]] in [[Peckham]], is an aspiring lawyer who works as a waiter for an upscale bar-restaurant. He interviews at Cathcarts and various smaller law firms, but is unable to get a job. At dinner with his wealthy girlfriend Bella and her friends, Johnny meets her childhood friend Angus, who is condescending towards his ambitions and failed employment attempts. After having to serve Angus while on a shift at the restaurant, Johnny is fired after punching Angus in the face. He interviews at Taylor & Byrne, the last job offer he has, the next day; Taylor & Byrne, desperate to get more talent, hire him as a junior lawyer for Carla's upcoming divorce case. Morgan meets with his own lawyers at Cathcarts and learns that Johnny is in fact a [[Mole (espionage)|mole]] secretly working for Cathcarts. Morgan flies down to Paris to join his wife at the premiere for ''The Milliner''; they barely speak while in the car. At the premiere, Carla gets served divorce papers by a Cathcarts staffer in the crowd. Now with both parties aware of each other's intentions, Morgan and Carla pose together for the cameras on the [[red carpet]].
 |LineColor       = BCBDBA
}}
{{Episode list
 |EpisodeNumber   = 2
 |Title           = No More Nasty Surprises
 |DirectedBy      = Ben Taylor
 |WrittenBy       = George Kay
 |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|10|8|df=y}}
 |ShortSummary    = The two sides gear up for a three-day [[mediation]] session between the couple, with each firm using the opportunity to get information on the other. During the first session, Morgan admits that his income has grown vastly since they married after Zephyr's valuation grew to hundreds of millions, which could void the couple's prenup due to a clause concerning a significant lifestyle change. Serena becomes convinced that Cathcarts found out about Carla's case through Flora and tries to get Flora to sign a [[non-disclosure agreement]] for her silence. Flora refuses to sign. On the second day, both sides get nowhere after multiple offers get rejected. Flora's mother Melinda shows up at Cathcarts, intending to meet with Serena, but is unable to reach her and leaves. Johnny meets Melinda and learns about the NDA and that Flora will not sign it unless they get twenty thousand pounds first. He relays this information to his contact at Cathcarts, senior partner David Schill, who figure out that Flora was set up by Carla. Johnny is sent to Flora and Melinda's home to get them to sign the NDA in exchange for getting a leak in their roof fixed. He confirms his success in a [[voicemail]] he sends to both Taylor & Byrne and David. At the last mediation session, Morgan and Carla confirm they want to go forward with [[arbitration]]. While at home with her mother, Flora texts Morgan to ask if she can see him again.
 |LineColor       = BCBDBA
}}
{{Episode list
 |EpisodeNumber   = 3
 |Title           = Chip Off the Block
 |DirectedBy      = Ben Taylor
 |WrittenBy       = Kelly Jones
 |OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2026|10|15|df=y}}
 |ShortSummary    = Carla picks up Gabe, her teenage son from a previous relationship, from the [[boarding school]] where he attends to inform him about the divorce. Gabe, who is distant from his mother and much closer with his stepfather, intuits that someone in the marriage was unfaithful. Trying to get the prenup voided but learning that a proper assessment of Morgan's income from a [[forensic accounting|forensic accountant]] would take weeks, Taylor & Byrne instead try to push the narrative that Carla had to reject major roles from blockbuster superhero franchises to be with her family. When they find that she was never offered these roles at all, Nicholas and Serena pivot that Morgan's close relationship with Gabe—whom he never formally adopted and therefore has no legal relationship with—counts as a significant lifestyle change. During a meeting with his advisors, Morgan learns that Carla cannot take his stock in Zephyr if he transfers his shares over to his financial advisor Gillian; he refuses the offer. Gabe takes a train to London to stay with Morgan, but angrily leaves when Morgan admits to infidelity, and goes to a raucous house party hosted by his friend Thibault. Carla initially calls Morgan to find her son, but Morgan is encouraged not to pick up by St. John. Out of options, she calls Johnny, who leaves Bella's [[black-tie]] work event to help Carla. Johnny finds Gabe at Thibault's home, drunk and bloodied from a fight, and opens up to him about his own parents' divorce. The next day, Gabe attends the couple's arbitration session at Taylor & Byrne's offices. When Morgan and Carla get in an argument over him, Gabe interrupts and storms out; Morgan is the only one who goes after him. With the arbitrator convinced that there is a significant lifestyle change, the prenup gets voided. Morgan calls Gillian to arrange the trade of his stock and opens a bottle of beer the exact same way that Gabe did.
 |LineColor       = BCBDBA
}}

==Production==
===Development===
[[Sky UK]] and co-producer [[HBO]] ordered two seasons of the series in an [[anthology]] format. [[George Kay (writer)|George Kay]] is the show's creator and showrunner with Ben Taylor as director. The series is produced by New Pictures and Observatory Pictures. Executive producers include Kay, Taylor, Willow Grylls, Matt Sandford, Susan Breen, Andrea Dewsbury and Megan Spanjian.<ref name="Release">{{cite web|accessdate=20 August 2025|url=https://deadline.com/2025/08/dominic-west-sienna-miller-war-hbo-sky-1236492735/|title=Dominic West & Sienna Miller To Star In Legal Thriller ''War'' For HBO & Sky From George Kay|website=Deadline Hollywood|date=20 August 2025|first=Peter|last=White|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260519180544/https://deadline.com/2025/08/dominic-west-sienna-miller-war-hbo-sky-1236492735/|archive-date=19 May 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Alongside Kay, the writers of the series include Kelly Jones, [[Jess Brittain]], [[Catherine Shepherd]], Yemi Oyefuwa and Krissie Ducker.<ref name=":0"/>

===Casting===
The cast of the first series is led by [[Dominic West]] and [[Sienna Miller]] with [[Phoebe Fox]], [[James McArdle]], [[Pip Torrens]], [[Nina Sosanya]] and [[Archie Renaux]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a65830533/sky-war-dominic-west-sienna-miller/ |title=New London-set "scandal-soaked legal thriller" packed with "twists and betrayal" confirmed|date=20 August 2025|website=Digital Spy|first=Joe|last=Anderton|accessdate=20 August 2025}}</ref> [[Nick Mohammed]], [[Celia Imrie]], [[Shaheen Jafargholi]], [[Akiya Henry]], [[Honor Swinton Byrne]], [[Miles Jupp]], [[Kartanya Maynard]], [[Alexandra Mardell]], Mark Quartley and [[Steve Furst]] have series regular roles, while [[Rose Williams (actress)|Rose Williams]], [[Camille Coduri]] and Aran Murphy joined the cast in guest roles for series one.<ref>{{cite web|website=Hollywood Reporter|accessdate=23 October 2025|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/war-legal-series-cast-slow-horses-nick-mohammed-1236406852/|title=HBO, Sky Legal Thriller ‘War’ Casts ‘Slow Horses’ Star Nick Mohammed, Celia Imrie|first=Georg|last=Szalai|date=22 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251022145726/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/war-legal-series-cast-slow-horses-nick-mohammed-1236406852/|archive-date=22 October 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2025, it was announced that [[Emma Laird]] joined the cast for series one.<ref>{{cite web|website=Deadline|accessdate=7 November 2025|url=https://deadline.com/2025/11/emma-laird-legal-thriller-war-dominic-west-sienna-miller-1236608880/|title=Emma Laird Joins HBO & Sky Legal Series ‘War’ With Dominic West & Sienna Miller|first=Georg|last=Szalai|date=6 November 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107022134/https://deadline.com/2025/11/emma-laird-legal-thriller-war-dominic-west-sienna-miller-1236608880/|archive-date=7 November 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

The cast of the second series is led by [[Marisa Tomei]], [[Kelly Macdonald]], [[David Harewood]] and [[Richard Schiff]], with [[Claire Skinner]], [[Omari Douglas]], [[Kadiff Kirwan]], [[Douglas Booth]], [[Charles Edwards (actor)|Charles Edwards]], [[Luca Pasqualino]], [[Rebecca Front]], [[Alexandra Maria Lara]], [[Linus Roache]], Violet Braeckman, [[Sasha Behar]], Sid Phoenix, Cornelius Booth and Megan Channell.<ref name=":0"/>

===Filming===
[[Principal photography]] began in September 2025, with filming taking place at the OMA X Film Studios, in [[Enfield, London]].<ref>{{cite web|website=Screen Daily|url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/2025-film-and-high-end-tv-productions-shooting-in-the-uk-and-ireland-latest-updates/5200306.article|title=2025 film and high-end TV productions shooting in the UK and Ireland: latest updates|first1=Diana|last=Lodderhose|date=29 September 2025|accessdate=1 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251016004330/https://www.screendaily.com/news/2025-film-and-high-end-tv-productions-shooting-in-the-uk-and-ireland-latest-updates/5200306.article|archive-date=16 October 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2026, it was announced that the filming of the first series had been wrapped in February and the second series would go into production.<ref>{{cite web|last=Yossman|first=K.J.|title=Marisa Tomei, Kelly Macdonald and David Harewood Set for Second Season of HBO, Sky Legal Drama ‘War’|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/marisa-tomei-kelly-macdonald-david-harewood-season-2-war-1236740698/|website=Variety|date=May 7, 2026|access-date=May 7, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808034300/https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/marisa-tomei-kelly-macdonald-david-harewood-season-2-war-1236740698/|archive-date=8 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Release ==
The series premiered on 1 October 2026 on [[HBO]] and 2 October 2026 on [[Sky Atlantic]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Kanter|first=Jake|title=''War'' First Look & Trailer: Dominic West & Sienna Miller Do Battle In HBO/Sky Divorce Drama|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/war-trailer-dominic-west-sienna-miller-hbo-sky-drama-1237027476/|website=Deadline Hollywood|date=6 August 2026|access-date=6 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806152531/https://deadline.com/2026/08/war-trailer-dominic-west-sienna-miller-hbo-sky-drama-1237027476/|archive-date=6 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==
On the review aggregator website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the series holds an approval rating of 87%, based on 47 reviews, with an average of rated reviews of 7.3/10. The website's critics consensus reads, "Taking on courtroom proceedings with stylish flair, this heady drama features captivating performances, biting dialogue, and an entertaining premise that proves all's fair in love and ''WAR''."<ref>{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=war_2026|type=tv|season=1|access-date=14 October 2026|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 74 out of 100 based on 27 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{Cite Metacritic|id=war|type=tv|season=1|access-date=14 October 2026|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
